question.leadin: This place was originally known as the Flavian Amphitheatre.
question.text: Name this structure which included 80 entrances. Its construction began under the emperor Vespasian [veh-SPAY-zhun] and was completed under the emperor Titus.
question.clue: The construction of a complex tunnel network at this structure, its hypogeum ("hy-PO-jee-um"), ended the prior practice of flooding this place for mock naval battles.

swap.text: This battle was a disastrous defeat of Hannibal by the Roman general Scipio Africanus. This battle was so detrimental to Carthage that it resulted in the immediate end of the Second Punic War.
swap.clue: The winning side eased through the first two lines of infantry, but the legionnaires could not muster the energy to defeat the third line.

question.text: This Roman farmer and statesman inspired the Third Punic War and sacking of Carthage by ending all of his speeches "Carthago delenda est," or "Carthage must be destroyed!"
question.clue: During a particularly brutal campaign in part of Hispania, this man apocryphally declared "the war feeds itself."

swap.text: After Teutoburg Forest, this emperor would periodically bash his head into a wall while yelling "Quinctilius Varus, give me back my legions!" This emperor won the Battle of Actium.
swap.clue: This ruler reportedly shouted at Quintilius Varus to "give me back my legions" after his forces lost the Battle of the Teutoburg Forest.

question.leadin: This civilization's capital of Veii ("VAY-ee") was sacked by the forces of Marcus Furius Camillus, and was legendarily led by king Lars Porsenna.
question.text: Name this ancient Italian civilization that was assimilated into the Roman republic.
question.answerHtml: Etruscans (“eh-TRUSS-kuhnz”) [or Rasenna; or Rasna; or Tusci; or Etrusci; or Turrhenoi; or Tursenoi; prompt on Tyrrheni or Tyrrhenians]
question.clue: These people were organized into the Dodecapoli, twelve cities that formed their namesake league.

swap.text: Mehmed defeated the 11th ruler of this name by destroying the capital of the Byzantine empire. That capital was named after another emperor of this name who adopted Christianity as the official Roman religion.
swap.clue: That emperor was the subject of a prophecy when Germanus witnessed him defecate in his baptismal font, and thus gained the nickname Copronymous.

question.leadin: After this emperor stepped down, he resided in a palace in Split and became a vegetable grower.
question.text: Name this Roman Emperor who formed the Tetrarchy during the 3rd century BCE, thus splitting up the Roman Empire.
question.clue: This emperor came to power after his predecessor, Carus, was killed by lightning in Persia, and he won the Battle of the Margus River to consolidate his power over rivals Carinus and Numerian.

swap.text: This author wrote the Lives of the Caesars about the first 11 emperors, as well as On Famous Men.
swap.clue: His account of an expulsion of the Jews from Rome refers to their taking up the customs of "Chrestus," who may be Christ.

question.leadin: As part of the Second Triumvirate, Lepidus received this office.
question.text: Name this chief priest of the Roman religion.
question.clue: Per the Lex Ogulnia, the plebeian Coruncanius held this position that Marcus Aurelius held instead of Lucius Verus.

swap.leadin: Name these women who bedeviled the Roman Empire.
swap.text: When this woman's husband Prasutagus died, Rome annexed his former kingdom, prompting this queen of the Iceni to lead a revolt in East Anglia that was put down by Paulinus.
swap.clue: This person's popularity as a patriotic symbol in Victorian Britain was influenced by the theory that her name comes from a root meaning "victory" in Celtic.

question.leadin: Identify these things related to the early days of Rome.
question.text: The revolt that resulted in Tarquinius' deposition was sparked by his son's rape of this woman.
question.clue: After that, a man threatened to place the naked corpse of a slave next to this woman's bed to frame her for adultery.

swap.leadin: This king legendarily purchased the three Syllibine Books after six of the original nine were burned in a negotiation ploy.
swap.text: Name this last king of Rome. This despot of Etruscan descent was overthrown after his son raped Lucretia.
swap.answerHtml: Tarquin the Proud [or Tarquinius Superbus; do not accept “Tarquinius Priscus”]
swap.clue: This man who usurped Servius Tullius to become king of Rome. He himself was popularly overthrown after his son Sextus raped a woman named Lucretia.

question.text: Before fleeing to the Balearics, Mago was defeated at this battle near Seville by a concealed force of Romans under Scipio Africanus. The battle of Baecula and this battle ended Carthaginian power in Spain.
question.clue: This battle's victor unusually placed legions on the wings and auxiliaries in the centre, later creating a concave formation that mirrored a battle occurring ten years prior.

swap.leadin: This woman was married to Prasutagus, whose will was ignored after he died.
swap.text: Name this queen of the Iceni tribe who revolted against her Roman oppressors at Camulodunum, but was eventually defeated by Suetonius Paulinus at Watling Street.
swap.clue: This person succeeded Prasutagus as the leader of the Iceni tribe and may have been inspired by to act by her public flogging and the rape of her daughters.

question.text: This very first pope is the patron saint of bakers and Las Vegas. He's often depicted standing at the gates of heaven allowing people in.
question.clue: Piux IX installed a statue of this first pope in his namesake basilica in the Vatican. As an apostle this man denied Jesus three times.

swap.text: The Senate perception of Maximinus's barbarism was partly inspired by his Carpi ancestry from this region. Aurelian abandoned this region whose past leaders, like Decebalus, fought wars against Trajan and Domitian.
swap.clue: Soldiers of this region used the sickle-like falx during a war in which a bridge near the Iron Gates was built by Apollodorus.

question.leadin: One part of this structure lends its name to the Vindolanda Tablets discovered in the 1970s.
question.text: Identify this structure whose archaeological remains can be found at sites like Brocolitia and Cilurnum.
question.clue: A birthday invitation was found on one of the Vindolanda tablets, which were unearthed near this structure.

swap.leadin: This law imposed a fine on those who held public land in excess of a certain prescribed limit, and ended discrimination against plebeians.
swap.text: Identify this constitutional reform of Roman law enacted in 367 B.C.E.

question.leadin: The rites of Bona Dea that Clodius scandalized by intruding on were hosted by this person.
question.text: Name this person who Clodius was supposedly trying to seduce before he was caught. Her husband defended his decision to divorce her as a result of the scandal by stating that Caesar's wife had to be beyond suspicion.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about what happens in times of emergency during the Roman Republic.
swap.text: Cicero's speech defending this man makes the correct assertion "In times of war the law falls silent." This man was responsible for the death of Publius Clodius Pulcher.
swap.clue: This man was accused of the murder of Publius Clodius Pulcher, but due to intimidation, Cicero failed to successfully defend him, and he was forced into exile.
